title: Querying Infinispan with Hibernate Search & Lucene Query Builder
subtitle: Building composable, type-safe full-text queries, boolean junctions, pagination, and sorting over distributed in-memory data grids.
overview: Querying data within distributed caches requires expressive APIs that go far beyond primitive key lookups. By leveraging Hibernate Search's integration with Infinispan, engineers can construct rich boolean queries, full-text token search, fuzzy matches, and sorted pagination over structured domain entities. This article provides patterns and code implementations for production search pipelines.
problem: In-memory key-value stores default to primary-key retrieval. As data grows, applications frequently need cross-entity filtering, full-text searches across multiple nested fields, and sorted pagination. Writing manual iterate-and-filter logic in application memory causes massive memory bloat and unacceptable latency.

│                            ▼                           │

│                            │                           │
│                            ▼                           │

└────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘

└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

implementation.title: 1. Search Manager Initialization & Statistics
implementation.description: Initialize the Infinispan SearchManager and enable search statistics to measure query duration, index latency, and execution plan metrics.

implementation.title: 2. Composable Boolean Junction Query Construction
implementation.description: Construct dynamic boolean search queries with should() (OR) and must() (AND) semantics over indexed fields.

implementation.title: 3. Pagination, Sorting & Result Hydration
implementation.description: Execute the compiled query through CacheQuery with sort specifications and boundary parameters to protect memory consumption.

impact: Delivered flexible full-text fuzzy search across clinical entities with sub-10ms response times.
Prevented out-of-memory faults by enforcing strict page-size bounds (`maxResults`) on all query endpoints.
Provided transparent metrics on index queries via SearchManager statistics.
lessons: Always specify `IndexedQueryMode.FETCH` only when full entity graphs are needed; use projected fields (`SKIP_LOADING`) for summary views to reduce object hydration overhead.
Ensure sort fields in entities are explicitly indexed as un-tokenized DocValues to avoid costly runtime field un-inverting in Lucene.
